**Step 0.5e (reviewer-isolation snapshot gate — L2, opt-in via `--isolate-reviewers`).** When reviewer isolation is enabled (flag-gated opt-in; OFF by default so today's #153 dirty-tree-audit behavior is unchanged), the wrapper grounds the two ClaudeProcess review children (the Tier-1 audit child and the adversarial scorer) in an isolated `git worktree` snapshot rather than the live shared worktree, so those children never read another session's mid-commit state; and — via L1 + L1b — no reviewer of any class can mutate the repository it is auditing (reliability / data-loss-prevention). (The text-in/out Tier-2 swarm workers still read the live tasklist path in v1 — see item 4 and the honest `snapshot-children-only` telemetry value; closing their read surface is the deferred "design (a)" follow-up.) The gate runs in the Python wrapper (`cli/reflect/{config,runner,ensemble}.py`) AFTER the dry-run gate (FR-12 unaffected), and proceeds:

1. **Cleanliness probe** — compute `audit_tree_dirty` = the tracked, in-scope (`git diff --name-only <base>`) paths that are dirty in `git status --porcelain=v1`. Untracked entries do not count. Fail-closed: any git error → treat as dirty.
2. **STOP-on-non-committable predicate (COR-1)** — `committable = base resolves AND HEAD resolves AND not audit_tree_dirty`. If NOT committable, the wrapper STOPs with `status: stopped-precondition` (verdict BLOCKED, exit 2 — the fail-closed contract is unchanged) and `reason ∈ {dirty, no-committable-ref, head-moved-precondition, snapshot-precleanup-failed, worktree-add-failed}` (any non-zero `git worktree add` exit STOPs with the captured stderr, never falling back to the live tree). It never points reviewers at a committed-ref snapshot that omits the uncommitted target.
3. **Snapshot creation (COR-2 / A-2)** — on the committable path, pre-clean a leftover `<output>/_review-snapshot`, re-resolve HEAD immediately before `git worktree add --detach <output>/_review-snapshot <ref>` and STOP `head-moved-precondition` on drift (the parallel-session HEAD-moved hazard), then create a REAL worktree checkout (NOT an archive, so serena/auggie stay indexed).
4. **Grounding-root redirect (scope: ClaudeProcess children only, v1)** — the snapshot grounds the two live-CWD review children: the Tier-1 audit child and the adversarial scorer both run with `cwd = <snapshot>`, never the live shared worktree. The text-in/out Tier-2 swarm workers hold NO repo CWD; in v1 their review target is still sourced from the live tasklist path (NOT yet derived from `<snapshot>`), so isolation covers the two ClaudeProcess children but not the swarm-worker read surface. The telemetry value `snapshot-children-only` (below) reports this scope honestly rather than overclaiming full `snapshot` isolation. (Closing the swarm-worker read surface — deriving their target from `<snapshot>` — is the deferred "design (a)" follow-up; the mutation incident vector is independently closed by L1 + L1b for every reviewer class regardless.)
5. **`finally` teardown (A-3)** — the snapshot is always removed via `git worktree remove --force` (never `rm -rf` / `git stash`), on success / STOP / exception, while the always-write sidecar still emits inside the try.

native plugin route, not the package wrapper. At Wave 0 select/reserve the frozen
input set; at Step 3B.0, AFTER T1/verification evidence exists and BEFORE any fixed
read-only reviewer is spawned, the ORCHESTRATOR provisions the actual snapshot.

1. Apply every pinned-output, explicit-input-overlap, traversal, symlink and plugin
   distribution guard FIRST. Create a fresh run output, never reuse a prior
   snapshot or delete intermediates. Keep snapshot files under this pinned output.
2. Enumerate the COMPLETE selected audit state into `<output>/selected-inputs.json`:
   explicit spec, optional tasklist, task-log/diff file, all in-scope changed files
   from the requested ref/diff, relevant dirty tracked files, relevant untracked/new
   files discovered from scoped `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` and the
   task log, linked evidence and needed dependency sources. Include existing/base
   evidence for deletions as captured diff/base artifacts; do not invent a current
   deleted file. Do not infer that `git diff` includes new files. Resolve narrowing
   scope against both changed paths AND new/log-declared paths. Freeze all files a
   reviewer may cite or inspect, not just the hunks. Missing/unreadable inputs or an
   incomplete enumeration block reviewer dispatch. Never copy `.git` or plugin
   distribution directories wholesale.
3. Schema: `{"enumeration_complete": true, "coverage_basis": "<requested diff,
   scope, dirty/new discovery and links>", "files": [{"source": "<absolute path>",
   "kind": "audit-input" | "run-evidence"}]}`. `run-evidence` is ONLY this run's
   already-written T1 card, coverage matrix, captured verification/base/diff and
   other ledgers under the pinned output; it is not an explicit user input and is
   not added to the audited input-tree hash. Every explicit user input stays
   subject to the original output/input overlap guard. Do not include the snapshot
   itself or later reviewer outputs in the selection. Supply the exact selection
   path to the recipe below. Capture current working-tree bytes, not HEAD-only.
4. Use the following stdlib recipe INLINE through native Bash, for example
   `uv run --no-project python - <repo-root> <pinned-output> <selection-json>` with
   the code block as stdin. It imports no package, installs nothing and writes no
   new production module. `uv` and `git` must actually be available to this
   orchestrator; otherwise report snapshot provisioning unavailable and STOP
   reviewer dispatch, never fall back to live roots. The recipe refuses stale
   output, symlinks and missing/non-regular inputs, captures before/copy/after
   SHA256 plus source Git inventory, retains a provenance manifest, and makes
   frozen copies read-only. A nonzero exit or non-verified manifest blocks dispatch.
5. Supply `reviewer_grounding_root: <output>/reviewer-snapshot/root` and
   `snapshot_kind: native-selected-inputs`, `native_reviewer_snapshot: verified`,
   `native_reviewer_snapshot_manifest_path: <output>/reviewer-snapshot/provenance-manifest.json`
   to every brief per `refs/reviewer-spec.md`. Do NOT emit wrapper
   `reviewer_isolation: snapshot-children-only`. Rewrite every source/evidence path
   through the manifest; no live-root fallback. An unindexed snapshot uses native
   Read/Grep/Glob with a loud MCP-unindexed degraded marker.
6. Run this SAME inline recipe with
   `uv run --no-project python - --verify <provenance-manifest>` immediately before
   dispatch and after reviewers finish. Source or frozen-copy hash mismatch means
   `input_drift` / `native_snapshot_drift`, `status: partial`, no acceptance of those
   reviewer findings and no promotion. Keep failed snapshots and intermediates;
   choose a new run/output for retry. No teardown deletion or package wrapper.

<!-- native-snapshot-recipe:start -->
```python
"""Task-owned source for the exact inline native snapshot recipe in the bundled skill."""

import hashlib
import json
import os
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def digest(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def under(path, root):
    return path == root or root in path.parents


def regular(path):
    if not path.is_absolute() or ".." in path.parts:
        raise ValueError("snapshot input must be an absolute, traversal-free path")
    if path.resolve(strict=True) != path or not stat.S_ISREG(path.lstat().st_mode):
        raise ValueError("snapshot input must be a regular file with no symlink components")
    return path.read_bytes()


def git_state(repo, output):
    command = ["git", "status", "--porcelain=v1", "-z", "--untracked-files=all", "--", "."]
    if under(output, repo):
        command.append(":(exclude)" + output.relative_to(repo).as_posix())
    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=repo, capture_output=True, check=True, timeout=30)
    return result.stdout.hex()


def verify(manifest_path):
    manifest = json.loads(regular(manifest_path))
    if manifest["status"] != "verified":
        raise ValueError("snapshot manifest was not verified")
    root = Path(manifest["reviewer_grounding_root"])
    if root.resolve(strict=True) != root:
        raise ValueError("snapshot root was retargeted")
    for row in manifest["files"]:
        snapshot = Path(row["snapshot_path"])
        if not under(snapshot, root):
            raise ValueError("manifest copy escapes snapshot root")
        if digest(regular(snapshot)) != row["sha256_copy"]:
            raise ValueError("snapshot copy changed: " + str(snapshot))
        if digest(regular(Path(row["source_path"]))) != row["sha256_after"]:
            raise ValueError("audited source changed: " + row["source_path"])
    return {"status": "verified", "reviewer_grounding_root": str(root), "files": len(manifest["files"])}


def provision(repo, output, selection_path):
    repo = repo.resolve(strict=True)
    output = output.resolve(strict=True)
    selection = json.loads(regular(selection_path))
    if selection.get("enumeration_complete") is not True or not selection.get("coverage_basis"):
        raise ValueError("explicit complete selected-input enumeration and coverage basis required")
    items = selection["files"]
    if not items:
        raise ValueError("empty snapshot selection")
    # All protocol output/input/distribution guards MUST already have passed.
    destination = output / "reviewer-snapshot"
    destination.mkdir(exist_ok=False)
    root = destination / "root"
    root.mkdir()
    manifest_path = destination / "provenance-manifest.json"
    manifest = {"status": "pending", "snapshot_kind": "native-selected-inputs", "source_repo_root": str(repo),
                "reviewer_grounding_root": str(root), "selection_path": str(selection_path),
                "selection_sha256": digest(regular(selection_path)), "coverage_basis": selection["coverage_basis"],
                "enumeration_complete": True, "files": []}
    try:
        before_state = git_state(repo, output)
        manifest["source_git_status_before_hex"] = before_state
        payloads = []
        seen = set()
        for item in items:
            source = Path(item["source"])
            kind = item["kind"]
            if kind not in ("audit-input", "run-evidence") or under(source, destination):
                raise ValueError("invalid source kind or recursive snapshot source")
            if kind == "audit-input" and under(source, output):
                raise ValueError("explicit audited input overlaps output")
            if kind == "run-evidence":
                if not under(source, output):
                    raise ValueError("run-evidence must be produced within pinned output")
                relative = Path("__run_evidence__") / source.relative_to(output)
            elif under(source, repo):
                relative = source.relative_to(repo)
                if relative.parts[0] in ("__external__", "__run_evidence__"):
                    raise ValueError("reserved snapshot namespace collision")
            else:
                relative = Path("__external__") / digest(str(source).encode()) / source.name
            target = root / relative
            if target in seen:
                raise ValueError("duplicate selected path or snapshot collision")
            seen.add(target)
            content = regular(source)
            payloads.append((source, target, kind, content))
        for source, target, kind, content in payloads:
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with target.open("xb") as handle:
                handle.write(content)
                handle.flush()
                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
            target.chmod(0o444)
            copied = digest(regular(target))
            before = digest(content)
            after = digest(regular(source))
            manifest["files"].append({"kind": kind, "source_path": str(source), "snapshot_path": str(target),
                                      "sha256_before": before, "sha256_copy": copied, "sha256_after": after})
            if not before == copied == after:
                raise ValueError("source/copy hash mismatch: " + str(source))
        # Re-read EVERY source after ALL copies, not merely just after its own copy.
        for row in manifest["files"]:
            if digest(regular(Path(row["source_path"]))) != row["sha256_before"]:
                raise ValueError("input changed during snapshot: " + row["source_path"])
        after_state = git_state(repo, output)
        manifest["source_git_status_after_hex"] = after_state
        if after_state != before_state or digest(regular(selection_path)) != manifest["selection_sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("selection or source git inventory changed during snapshot")
        manifest["status"] = "verified"
        for folder in sorted((path for path in root.rglob("*") if path.is_dir()), reverse=True):
            folder.chmod(0o555)
        root.chmod(0o555)
    except Exception as error:
        manifest["status"] = "failed"
        manifest["failure_reason"] = str(error)
        raise
    finally:
        # Preserve failed and successful snapshots/intermediates; NEVER teardown.
        manifest_path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n")
    return verify(manifest_path)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        if sys.argv[1] == "--verify":
            result = verify(Path(sys.argv[2]))
        else:
            result = provision(Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]), Path(sys.argv[3]))
        print(json.dumps(result))
    except Exception as error:
        print(json.dumps({"status": "failed", "reason": str(error)}))
        raise SystemExit(1)
```

This distribution runs without the Python package, global framework installation,
project development mirrors, or other plugins. Resolve all file reads from this
plugin: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/<directory>/SKILL.md` and
`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/agents/<filename>.md`. A `refs/<file>` path is relative to
the loaded skill directory, never the audited project's working directory.
Frontmatter logical names do not override native filename/directory identities.
Use the qualified names below for EVERY delegation, including tables and shorthand
`Task(...)` directives. Do not scan global directories, install dependencies, or
substitute an all-tools reviewer when a registered resource is absent.

# Confidence Calibrator — Independent Reflection Rubric Scoring

## Triggers

- Delegated via `Task(sc:confidence-calibrator)` by `sc:sc-reflect-protocol` in Wave 1D and independently for EVERY Tier-2 card in Wave 3C.
- This bundled agent is reflection-specific, not the six-dimension troubleshooting calibrator. Never auto-activate from conversational keywords.

## Role and independence

You are deliberately stripped of the card-formation context. You did not run the
grounding queries, draft the brief or iterate on the findings. Read only the
finished card, the supplied reflection rubric and cited artifacts needed to
spot-check its evidence. Do not receive the upstream investigative trail or other
reviewers' scores. Self-reported confidence is narrative, NEVER an input or a
starting point. Score one dimension at a time against the rubric anchors, not
social judgement about the upstream agent. A sharp divergence is a signal to
report honestly, not a reason to split the difference.

**DO NOT modify, edit, delete, move, or rename ANY file.** The orchestrator Writes
`output_path` from your returned report. You do not Write. Tools, model preference,
turn limit and `permissionMode: plan` remain the source's read-only contract.

## Inputs

- `card_path`: absolute path to the finished reflection card.
- `rubric_path`: absolute path to `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/sc-reflect-protocol/refs/reflection-rubric.md`; resolve from the plugin root, never global/project mirrors.
- `card_tier`: 1 or 2.
- `flags_context`: caller's reflection flags, including tier/depth/no-escalate restrictions; these do not alter the calibrated number.
- `output_path`: where the ORCHESTRATOR persists your returned report.
- `now_iso` (optional): supplied ISO-8601 timestamp. Omit Timestamp and note `input_absent: now_iso` when absent; never invent a clock.

## Responsibilities

1. Read the actual reflection rubric at `rubric_path` before the card. Require its FIVE dimensions and arithmetic mean. Missing, unreadable or incompatible rubric means `calibration_failed: true`, `calibrated: null`, and an explicit reason; never invent a rubric or use the troubleshooting formula.
2. Read `card_path`. Missing/empty/unparseable card means calibration failure with an explicit reason. A readable but incomplete card scores each unsupported dimension at 0.00 with Notes; absence of evidence is not weak evidence.
3. **Spot-check evidence citations** by Reading each cited file at its cited range. Do not trust quoted snippets. A mismatch is recorded and drives Citation grounding. Remote URLs cannot be checked with Read: record `spot_check_unverifiable: <url>` for EACH remote citation. Do not cap on URL presence alone or pretend it was verified; apply the supplied anchors to the actual evidence.
4. Score each dimension in `0.00-1.00` using the rubric's actual anchor bands:
   - Citation grounding
   - Coverage completeness
   - Deviation-classification clarity
   - Risk surface coverage
   - Recommendation actionability
   Classification uses exactly Authorized / Necessary / Drift / Regression, with Grounding Gaps separate, not a fifth class. Apply the rubric's contracted-sink evidence guidance within these five dimensions, not a sixth dimension.
5. Compute `C = (citation_grounding + coverage_completeness + deviation_classification_clarity + risk_surface_coverage + recommendation_actionability) / 5`, rounded to two decimals. Show all five inputs and the unrounded mean. No six-dimension troubleshooting gates, runtime-check cross-tab, verdict-direction caps or troubleshooting C-rule caps apply to reflection.
6. Return the score and delta. `C < 0.85` recommends ESCALATE; `C >= 0.85` returns `ORCHESTRATOR_DECIDES`, since the full priority table additionally requires scope/domain/density/coverage and asymmetric flags. The strict ceiling remains 0.90, medium floor 0.85. Never infer missing structural signals or override explicit tier/depth restrictions. The orchestrator owns the complete reflection routing rules.

## Output Format

```markdown
# Calibration Report

**Card under calibration**: <abs path>
**Rubric**: <abs path>
**Card tier**: <1|2>
**Timestamp**: <copy now_iso; omit when absent>
**calibration_failed**: false

## Per-dimension scores

| Dimension | Score | Justification (cite card content and verified evidence) |
|-----------|-------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| Citation grounding | <0.00-1.00> | <evidence> |
| Coverage completeness | <0.00-1.00> | <evidence> |
| Deviation-classification clarity | <0.00-1.00> | <evidence> |
| Risk surface coverage | <0.00-1.00> | <evidence> |
| Recommendation actionability | <0.00-1.00> | <evidence> |

## Calculation trace

- Five inputs: <list>
- Unrounded arithmetic mean: <value>
- **Calibrated**: <rounded C>
- **Self-reported**: <card value or absent; NOT used in score>
- **Delta**: <signed difference or null if self-report absent; explain>

## Escalation recommendation

- Recommendation: ESCALATE | ORCHESTRATOR_DECIDES
- Reason: <C below 0.85, or full structural routing belongs to orchestrator>
- Execution restrictions: <literal flags_context restrictions or none>

## Notes

- Citation mismatches and EACH `spot_check_unverifiable: <url>`.
- Missing sections, malformed inputs and all absent optional inputs.
```

On missing/incompatible rubric or unusable card, return the same report identity
with `calibration_failed: true`, `calibrated: null`, and the explicit failure
reason instead of fabricated scores. The orchestrator records a crash, timeout
or malformed output and may take ONLY the source-defined loud
`calibration: inline-fallback`; it must not claim independent calibration ran.

## Boundaries

Will score independently, cite each score's basis, spot-check real citations,
and return a number even when it sharply contradicts the self-report. Will NOT
rewrite the card, propose fixes/new evidence, inherit narrative framing, score
from intuition, or mutate files. Model-class selection stays with the
orchestrator's unchanged reflection disjoint-set rule: select a class outside
the reviewer classes when available, otherwise emit `calibrator_diversity:
degraded`. Every Tier-2 card uses its own independent instance in parallel.

## Failure Modes

- Crash/timeout/malformed output: orchestrator's explicit inline fallback, never silent success.
- Truncated readable card: missing dimensions score 0.00 with Notes; unusable card fails as above.
- Placebo risk: matching inline scores within ±0.05 does not establish independence or quality. Source meta-eval guidance is maintainer-only, not a bundled runtime dependency.
